sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Distribution of Excess Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors and Resistors

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified civil and commercial law, with common-law-informed fiduciary jurisprudence applicable to Private Interest Foundations and trusts)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012, includes investment chapter)
Panama–Canada Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 April 2013, includes investment chapter)
European Union–Central America Association Agreement (commercial and investment provisions in force for Panama since 2012)
Panama–Mexico Free Trade Agreement (in force, maintained)
Panama–Colombia Partial Scope Agreement / FTA (in force)
Panama–Singapore Double Taxation Agreement (comprehensive DTA, in force 2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Act), as amended by the 2015 transparency reforms requiring disclosure of founder, council, and protector identity to the registered agent; Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (consolidated Panamanian AML/CFT statute creating the Unidad de Análisis Financiero 'UAF' and mandating CDD/EDD on regulated fiduciaries), as amended; Executive Decree No. 128 of 21 May 2019 (implementing regulations obliging registered agents to identify, verify, and file beneficial ownership of foundations); Law 5 of 17 January 2019 (statutory Beneficial Owner Register 'RUBF' administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos with restricted governmental access); FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 as applied by Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva / Escritura de Fundación) executed before a Panamanian Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / official charter documents of the corporate founder, if any, or notarized identity document of the natural person founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or civil registry of the founder's jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Panamanian Registered Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the founder's jurisdiction of origin, authenticated by apostille or, in non-Hague Convention states, by the Panamanian consular office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and address verification for each foundation council member, protector, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consular, notarial, or banking authorities of the respective countries of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for certified copies; bank-verified copies deemed equivalent under Law 23 of 2015

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional or banking reference letters covering source of funds and professional standing of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or reputable counsel of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private transmission with remote verification; apostille not required under Panamanian client due diligence practice

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all founders, council members, protectors, beneficiaries, and connected parties against (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (ii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and UK OFSI consolidated list; (iv) Panama's Official National List of Designated Persons and Associated Assets (Lista Nacional); and (v) international PEP databases maintained by commercial screening providers. Any PEP status, FATF high-risk jurisdiction nexus, or sanctions match triggers mandatory Enhanced Due Diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, written compliance approval, and, where required, reporting to the UAF under Law 23 of 2015 and Executive Decree 128 of 2019.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended; complemented by Law 32 of 1927 (Corporate Law), applicable to general commercial obligations; Title on Foundations at the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Foundation Section (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva) embodied in a notarized Escritura Pública and internal Regulations (Reglamento)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Foundation must hold an initial endowment of at least US$10,000.00 or its equivalent in another currency, as declared in the Foundation Charter; capital may be contributed in cash or in kind and must be identified for AML/KYC verification; no statutory escrow account is required, but the Resident Agent may request proof of funding.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Founder subscribes and contributes the initial lawful endowment of ten thousand United States Dollars (US$10,000.00) to the Foundation, which the Foundation Council hereby accepts. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Foundation is established at [address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and the Resident Agent is appointed to maintain all foundation records at such address. RESOLVED, that the following persons are elected to the Foundation Council for the first term: [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Protector, each with powers to act. RESOLVED, that the Council officers are authorized to open bank accounts, sign agreements, and initiate all regulatory filings necessary to conduct wholesale distribution of passive electronic components.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Foundation Charter and Internal Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama (Notaría Pública) in coordination with a licensed Panamanian corporate attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney to prepare the Foundation Charter and Internal Regulations in Spanish, including the foundation name, principal purpose, initial endowment, registered office address, resident agent, Foundation Council members, protector, and succession rules. Submit the draft for notarial review and obtain the proposed foundation name from the Public Registry to ensure availability.
required_dossiers: Proposed foundation name (with up to three alternate options)
Passport or ID copies of the Founder and Foundation Council members
Proof of registered office lease or address
AML/KYC questionnaires completed for all officers and the resident agent
Initial endowment bank statement or asset declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry returns a name conflict or objection, revise the foundation name via a name-reservation amendment and resubmit for notarial approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Execution of the Escritura Pública
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange for all parties to appear before the Notary Public to sign the Foundation Charter and Internal Regulations. The notary will authenticate the signatures, declare the legal capacity of the signatories, and issue the Escritura Pública number needed for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Executed Foundation Charter
Executed Internal Regulations
Notarial fee payment receipt
Identification documents of appearing parties
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of a notarial omission or signature irregularity, request the notary to execute a corrective addendum and re-notarize the document before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Foundation Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original Escritura Pública and the Internal Regulations to the Foundation Section, together with the written acceptance of the Resident Agent. Pay the registry fee (approximately US$350.00) at the cashier or via the official online portal. The registry will review the documents, assign a digital folio, and issue a provisional registration entry.
required_dossiers: Original Escritura Pública issued by the Notary
Original or certified copy of Internal Regulations
Resident Agent acceptance form
Copy of the Resident Agent's license
Registry fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or objection, correct the flagged articles within 30 calendar days through a notarial clarification or amendment; if the deadline is missed, restart the filing with a new presentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Registered Foundation Certificate and Tax Identification Number (RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama and General Directorate of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos, DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Public Registry approves the registration, request the certified Certificate of Registered Foundation. Then apply to the DGI for the Tax Identification Number (RUC) using the foundation certificate and the notarial deed; execute the sworn tax registration statement and obtain the RUC certificate for future invoicing and customs operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Foundation issued by the Public Registry
Certified copy of the Escritura Pública
Identification of the Foundation Council members
Proof of registered address
DGI registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI delays or rejects the RUC application, provide the DGI with a certified copy of the registry entry and correct any mismatches in the foundation purpose to align with the declared wholesale distribution activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operational Notice and Optional Occupational Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Municipio de Panamá) and Panama Social Security Fund (Caja de Seguro Social, CSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación with the municipality to obtain the local business license for commercial distribution; if the foundation will hire employees, register with the CSS as an employer and report occupational safety compliance. The distribution of passive electronic components is a non-industrial activity; no industrial operating permit is triggered, but the municipal license must be renewed annually.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Certificate of Registered Foundation
Lease agreement or ownership proof of the registered office/warehouse
Aviso de Operación application
Employer registration forms (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality questions the classification, present the ISIC code (4652) designation and the foundation charter confirming wholesale distribution, then apply for a revisory municipal ruling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the business scope (ISIC 4652, wholesale distribution of passive electronic components) does not constitute an industrial or manufacturing activity requiring a Panamanian industrial operating permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business License (Aviso de Operación) is the only applicable operating clearance, issued by the Municipality of Panama.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (MiAMBIENTE), Directorate of Environmental Quality and Management
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – commercial distribution with no manufacturing, discharge, or emission operations; no EIA Report or Environmental Registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; if a warehouse is used, the operator must comply with municipal solid waste disposal ordinances and minimum noise levels under CSTP (Código Sanitario de Panamá); no industrial wastewater discharge limits are implicated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá is required for the leased warehouse or office premises; structural load inspection and municipal building safety approval are required for any storage area; occupational health clearance and employee hazard training are required under CSS and the Ministry of Labor regulations if personnel are hired.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (Panama); electronic portal: SITIO e-Tax (https://etax.gob.pa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-founded Private Interest Foundation (PIF), the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) is obtained as follows: (1) execute and register the foundation deed (acta de fundación) with the Registro Público de Panamá; (2) appoint a resident agent (abogado idóneo) with continuing legal capacity; (3) file the electronic registration application through SITIO e-Tax requesting a RUC under the territorial-source taxpayer segment; (4) attach the registered foundation deed, identification of the foundation council (Consejo de la Fundación), and the authenticated appointment of the resident agent; (5) obtain the taxpayer's digital signature (firma electrónica) and DGI user credentials; and (6) open a US-dollar bank account in Panama to support payment rails and remittance certificates. A purely passive PIF holding foreign assets with no Panamanian-source activity is not ordinarily required to hold a RUC; registration becomes mandatory upon the first taxable act (ITBMS invoicing, customs declarations, or receipt of Panamanian-source income).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a check-the-box election. The PIF is mandatorily classified as a separate juridical person taxed only on Panamanian-source income under Law 25 of 1995 and the territorial rules of the Código Fiscal. Available practical elections include: (i) income tax computation under the standard net-income method versus the statutory alternative minimum method established by Law 66 of 2017 and DGI regulations; (ii) voluntary ITBMS registration when the PIF purchases local inputs and intends to recover input VAT against zero-rated exports; (iii) advance pricing agreement applications to the DGI for transfer-pricing certainty; and (iv) election of monthly instalment payment methods for corporate income tax. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are governed by BEPS-aligned general anti-avoidance and economic-substance provisions; no per-entity hybrid classification election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios – ITBMS)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 0 – no statutory economic turnover threshold; ITBMS registration is mandatory upon the first taxable act performed in Panama. A simplified small-taxpayer regime is available where annual gross receipts do not exceed approximately B/. 36,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under the Sistema de Facturación Electrónica (SFE) operated by the DGI. All active taxpayers, including PIFs engaged in taxable supplies, must issue invoices through DGI-authorized service providers (Proveedores de Servicios de Facturación Electrónica – PSFE). Each invoice is generated in XML format with a unique fiscal control number, transmitted via REST/SOAP API integration or the SFE web portal, validated near-real-time by the DGI, and stamped with a digital security code (código de seguridad). Export transactions are declared with the export code, and supporting declarations are filed with the Servicio Nacional de Aduanas (SNA).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A PIF distributing excess multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors qualifies for the 0% ITBMS rate where the goods leave Panamanian customs territory (FOB, CIP, or equivalent delivery terms to a foreign buyer) and title and risk pass outside Panama. The zero rate also extends to directly attributable logistics or freight services physically executed in Panama in connection with the export shipment. Input VAT properly attributable to zero-rated exports is creditable monthly and refundable by the DGI upon substantiated quarterly reconciliations. Domestic resale of the same goods to Panamanian customers is standard-rated at 7%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera – DUA) accepted and stamped by the Servicio Nacional de Aduanas (SNA)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal of the capacitors/resistors from Panamanian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa / bank deposit certificate) issued by the Panamanian banking institution
Certified SNA cargo manifest (manifiesto de carga) where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may reopen zero-rated export claims for 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of omission or fraud. If export substantiation is deficient, the 7% ITBMS is retroactively assessed with default interest and late-payment surcharges; fines range from 50% to 300% of the evaded tax under Articles 737–748 of the Código Fiscal. Willful falsification, sham export documentation, or failure to repatriate export proceeds is criminally prosecuted under Law 76 of 2019 (Régimen Penal Tributario), carrying imprisonment of up to 8 years, disqualification of foundation council members, and seizure of exported inventory proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — Panama has no conventional central bank or dedicated foreign exchange administration. Monetary and banking regulatory authority resides in the SBP; Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) acts solely as fiscal agent of the State. The U.S. dollar is legal tender and effective monetary policy is delegated to the U.S. Federal Reserve system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital account. The Panamanian Balboa (PAB) is a purely nominal unit pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and circulates only as fractional coinage; U.S. dollar banknotes are the circulating medium. There are no capital controls, no exchange-rate licensing, no prior-approval requirements for dividend distributions, loan repayments, royalty remittances, or trade settlements, and no restrictions on holding balances or contracting credit in any foreign currency. A territorial-tax-resident PIF engaged in passive electronic component distribution therefore operates with zero convertibility friction and effectively zero FX settlement risk in USD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panamanian law imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export or trade proceeds. Export proceeds may be retained offshore or in any currency. The only binding compliance constraints are AML-driven: cash and international wire transactions of USD 10,000 or more are reportable by the financial institution to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) under Ley 41 de 2007 and Ley 23 de 2015; SBP Acuerdo 008-2020 additionally mandates complete originator and beneficiary information on all cross-border remittances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account — statutory minimum endowment deposit (USD 10,000 under Law 25 de 1995) and sovereign-adjacent settlement account
Operational Account — trade receivables collection, supplier wire disbursements, and daily treasury concentration
Operational Account — USD current account with strong correspondent bank coverage in the U.S. and Asia-Pacific
Operational Account — secondary settlement account and collateralization of revolving trade credit lines
Trade Finance Account — import commercial letters of credit, standby LCs, and short-term import financing
Operational Account — tertiary concentration account with multi-currency sweep capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium — legally constrained. Panama has no dedicated electronic money institution (EMI) or neobank license; Ley 81 de 2019 regulates low-value payment service providers but the SBP has not issued a general-purpose EMI charter. Accordingly, foreign digital EMIs (e.g., U.S. or E.U.-licensed platforms) are not SBP-supervised and cannot independently serve as the PIF's primary treasury counterparty; they cannot provide regulated deposits nor the target 'Credit_Line' rail in Panama. EMIs remain viable as supplementary, low-balance collection and payables channels for the Asia-Pacific electronic components trade, with mandatory weekly sweeps to the primary Panamanian bank account to preserve audit trail integrity and avoid UAF red-flag concentration in unregulated accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the non-resident founder and at least one authorized signatory/council member of the PIF. Panamanian Tier-1 banks require an in-person interview at the branch in Panama City, biometric verification, and wet-ink signatures on the account opening package; fully remote electronic onboarding is not available for newly-created foreign-owned foundation accounts. The resident agent (licensed Panamanian law firm or fiduciary) may coordinate the appointment and present the Public Registry certification, but cannot substitute for the beneficial owner's physical interview except in rare, bank-approved mitigations via apostilled power of attorney combined with enhanced due diligence. Standard onboarding timelines are 2–4 weeks following UAF beneficial-ownership verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation structure with possible nominal ownership opacity: nominee or law-firm-affiliated council members obscuring ultimate beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Acto Constitutivo (Foundation Charter) and any private Reglamento; current Registro Público certificate of formation; UAF beneficial-ownership registration confirmation (Ley 41 de 2007 and SBP Acuerdo 008-2020) identifying all classes of beneficiaries; passport copies, professional CVs, and references for the founder, council members, and any protector; a written commercial-substance memorandum describing the ISIC 4652 distribution activity and expected counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contribution from a non-resident founder exceeding USD 50,000 flagged as unexplained wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete source-of-funds file: founder's bank reference letter, tax or audited financial statements supporting wealth accumulation, employment or business income documentation, notarized resolution of the foundation council authorizing the capital contribution, and a funds-deployment plan tied to the purchase of multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) and resistors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border supplier payments to Asia-Pacific component brokers with irregular invoice or shipping patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level commercial package: signed purchase order, supplier invoice with full bank identifiers, material certificates, freight-forwarder bill of lading or airway bill, and the Panama Customs (SIGA) electronic entry evidencing physical movement of the electronic inventory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Leveraged distribution company without dedicated staff: credit line request revealing thin operating substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month cash-flow forecast with inventory turnover and gross margin analysis; third-party warehouse inventory sub-ledger; audited financial statements prepared by a Panamanian licensed public accountant; commercial lease or logistics services contract; supplier and customer concentration reports; foundation council resolutions granting express borrowing authority.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: inbound USD capital contribution routed via SWIFT MT103 from the founder's or foundation-controlled account to the PIF's primary operational account at a Tier-1 Panamanian bank. Field 70 (Remittance Information) must read: 'CONTRIBUCION DE CAPITAL — FUNDACION DE INTERES PRIVADO — [Registro Público folio number] — NON-BORROWING'. Originator should match the founder recorded in the Acto Constitutivo to preserve territorial tax treatment (Código Fiscal, territorial-source principle) and to avoid third-party-loan misclassification. Panama imposes no statutory wire purpose-code system, but banks apply UAF reporting thresholds (USD 10,000) and SBP Acuerdo 008-2020 travel-rule data standards. A credit to the BNP Capital Escrow Account validates the statutory USD 10,000 minimum foundation endowment required at constitution under Law 25 de 1995. Capital contributions are non-taxable, non-VATable events and should be reflected as foundation equity, not revenue.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 for open-account settlement of supplier invoices for multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors, debited from the Banistmo or Banco General current account with value dating T+1. Documentary trade rail: Commercial Letters of Credit issued in favor of Asia-Pacific suppliers under UCP 600, transmitted via SWIFT MT700 with amendments via MT707 and negotiation evidence via MT754; required documents include commercial invoice, packing list, and transport document. The 'Credit_Line' rail is executed through a revolving short-term import financing line at BAC International Bank or Multibank, secured by inventory sub-ledger assignments or standby LCs, with USD settlement cleared over Fedwire/CHIPS via the Panamanian bank's U.S. nostro account. Domestic Panama USD clearing of low-value payments is supported by the local ACH system regulated under Ley 81 de 2019.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (1-week to 12-month tenors) against USD in EUR, CNY, JPY, and KRW
Window forwards for monthly supplier cash-flow rollovers on imported electronic components
FX swaps (swap de divisas) for short-term liquidity conversion between USD and EUR or JPY
Cross-currency swaps with international bank counterparties to align EUR payables with USD funding
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted currencies such as offshore CNY and KRW, executed offshore given the shallowness of the Panamanian interbank market
Vanilla FX call and put options at eligible international dealing desks for tail-risk management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax / Tasa Única Anual renewal for Panama Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 May, regardless of the foundation’s incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge plus monthly default interest; persistent non-payment results in DGI non-compliance status, denial of good-standing certificates, and potential administrative strike-off of the foundation by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales – RBF) update or annual agent re-confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI – Registro de Beneficiarios Finales platform, through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of any change in ultimate beneficial ownership; if no change, annual confirmation must be captured in the agent’s compliance file at the time of the May 31 franchise tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update or confirm UBO data subjects the foundation to administrative fines under Panama’s beneficial ownership regime and may suspend access to official certificates until the registry is corrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office standing confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed registered agent (private act; effective before Registro Público when agent changes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuously in force; renewed annually and must be effective prior to the May 31 franchise tax deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of registered agent or office is a statutory violation; the Registro Público may administratively strike off the foundation, and it cannot execute legal acts or obtain tax certificates until a licensed agent is reinstated.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a Private Interest Foundation that is passive, privately held, operates from foreign sources, and does not carry on commercial or financial activity in Panama. A certified audit becomes mandatory if the foundation’s charter so stipulates, if it engages in Panama-source economic activity and is categorized as a large taxpayer / Gran Contribuyente, if an explicit order is issued by the DGI or a court, or if the foundation voluntarily elects to prepare audited financial statements for stakeholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Panama (NIIF); a non-commercial PIF may retain simplified cash-basis records for asset administration, but any formal or locally required financial statements must conform to NIIF.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Panama PIF has no shareholders; the substance of the UBO confirmation is identification of the foundation's settlor, council, and beneficiaries. The DGI-run RBF record must be updated within 15 days of any change. At each annual franchise tax renewal on or before May 31, the registered agent must re-confirm that the recorded beneficial ownership and the foundation's charter data remain accurate; if the agent has received a signed written declaration of no-change from the foundation council, the annual confirmation may be limited to that declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation constitutive deed and any amendments (Escritura Pública) retained by registered agent
Register of Foundation Council members (directors) with appointments, resignations, and powers
Minute Book of resolutions of the Foundation Council
Beneficial owner registration file with DGI and registered-agent KYC records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – 1,500 per year depending on service level (registered office, RBF management, secretarial and legal support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 7,500 only if a certified audit is triggered; ordinarily USD 0 for a passive PIF without Panama-source operations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial system: only Panamanian-source income is taxable. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) engaged in the distribution of electronic passive components is subject to the general 25% corporate rate on its net Panamanian-source profits. Foreign-source income is exempt. No statutory tax holidays; however, income derived from exports abroad may be treated as foreign-source if not sourced to a Panama PE. Free-zone incentives (e.g., Panama-Pacifico) apply only where a physical licence is held, not assumed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 106 (Declaración Jurada del Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas); filed electronically via DGI e-Tax (Oficina Virtual) at etax.mef.gob.pa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months following the fiscal year end; for calendar-year accounts, due on or before 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross taxable income from Panamanian-source sales of electronic components and connected logistics services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficiaries do not file; the PIF itself reports all gross revenue attributable to Panamanian economic activity. Foreign-source turnover is excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and deductions (including related-party inventory purchases after transfer-pricing adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must prove arm's length pricing and be supported by TP documentation; non-resident suppliers are not required to file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, commissions, depreciation and amortization attributable to Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to foreign affiliates must be properly documented and may be re-characterised if substance requirements are not met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (Renta Neta Gravable) after deducting expenses and applying loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the net figure subject to the 25% rate; the return may be filed as a nil return if only foreign-source income has been generated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable (25% of Box 4) and any monthly prepayments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To claim treaty exemption or a reduced rate on related items, attach a valid Panama TRC and treaty relief forms before the due date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fine of 5% of the tax due per month up to 50%, plus monthly interest (currently 1%) and an administrative surcharge of USD 100 minimum. Understatement due to fraud can trigger penalties of 100%–300% of the evaded tax and criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (statutory rate on dividends/distributions paid out of Panamanian-source taxable profits; distributions by a non-commercial PIF are not treated as dividends).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA, the non-resident or local payer must file Form 280 (Solicitud de Trato Tributario) with the DGI before payment, present a Panama Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued for that calendar year, and provide evidence of beneficial ownership. The payer may apply the treaty rate at the time of remittance only after approval; otherwise excess WHT may be reclaimed via refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory gross-basis WHT: royalties 12.5%, technical service fees 15%, interest on external financing 5% (general) or 8% (negotiable instruments). Under most Panamanian DTAs, royalty WHT is reduced to 5% and interest WHT to 0%–5%, subject to fulfilment of substance and TRC conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 1,000,000 in controlled transactions per fiscal year triggers the Local File; Master File is required when group annual consolidated revenue exceeds USD 50,000,000. Panama uses the US dollar as legal tender.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not maintain a general Economic Substance Regulation; however, the PIF must maintain effective management, local accounting records, an appointed Foundation Council, and a Panama Resident Agent. For treaty residence and to avoid anti-abuse recharacterisation, the PIF must demonstrate substantive business functions (inventory management, distribution, invoicing) in Panama rather than being a mere passthrough.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful submission of a Form 106 that understates Panamanian-source distribution turnover, records fictitious purchases from related non-resident suppliers, or claims non-existent deductible expenses to reduce the 25% taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion penalties under Código Fiscal: imprisonment from 2 to 5 years and a pecuniary fine of not less than the evaded tax, up to 300%; the tax authority may also apply civil charges and attach bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members and signatories are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax; prosecutorial seizure of personal assets, judicial travel bans, and possible extradition in cross-border cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a paper distribution company with no employees, no warehouse, and no local decision-making; using low-margin invoicing to shift electronic-components inventory profits to low-tax offshore affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of intercompany deductions, imposition of transfer-pricing penalties of up to 1% per month on undocumented transactions, cancellation of the tax-residency certificate, and inclusion of the PIF in published shell-company risk lists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be made liable for unpaid taxes and penalties; repeated non-substantive operation can trigger criminal charges of aiding tax fraud, with travel bans and up to 4 years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining undisclosed ultimate beneficial owners behind the PIF while channelling payment rails (SWIFT wires and credit-line receipts) for electronic inventory transactions connected to high-risk jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Banco Nacional de Panama / UAF enforcement under Law 23 of 2015: fines up to USD 5,000,000, suspension of registration, and criminal money-laundering penalties of 5–12 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal asset forfeiture, freezing orders, travel restrictions, and piercing of the foundation's legal veil to confiscate proceeds where the Foundation Council knowingly enabled laundering.
